title: Body process words
blurb: Name what the body is doing in HESI A2 words, from ingest to excrete, and never swap excrete/secrete, dilate/dilute or aspirate/expectorate.
question: A chart says a patient may aspirate when she eats, has poor perfusion in her feet and has not voided since morning. What is happening in each case?

teach.h: Process words are verbs of the body
teach.body: Formally, body process words name the actions and changes of normal and abnormal physiology: taking in, breaking down, releasing, moving air and blood, clotting and growing. In plain English: they say what the body is doing. Most are verbs, and many come in pairs that differ by one sound (excrete/secrete, ingest/digest, perfusion/profusion), which is exactly where HESI A2 distractors come from.

teach.h: Scenario: Aaliyah reads a nursing note
teach.body: Aaliyah Johnson, a dietary aide applying to a respiratory therapy program, reads: 'Patient may aspirate thin liquids; expectorating thick sputum. Poor perfusion to both feet. Has not voided since 6 a.m. Muscle atrophy in left leg after immobilization.' She translates: liquids may go down into the airway; she is coughing up mucus; blood flow to the feet is poor; she has not urinated since early morning; and the left leg muscles have wasted away from disuse.

teach.text: Excrete (get rid of waste) is not secrete (release a useful product: glands secrete hormones). Ingest (swallow) is not digest (break down). Aspirate (into the airway) is not expectorate (coughed out). Dilate (widen) is not dilute (weaken with liquid). Perfusion (blood flow) is not profusion (abundance). Atrophy (shrink) is the opposite of hypertrophy (enlarge).

items: Ingest = swallow in; masticate = chew; digest = break down; absorb = take in; metabolize = process.
Excrete = eliminate waste; secrete = produce and release; void = urinate; defecate = pass feces.
Aspirate = into the airway; expectorate = cough up and spit; ventilate = move air in and out.
Dilate = widen; constrict = narrow; coagulate = clot; perfusion = blood flow through tissue.
Atrophy = waste away; hypertrophy = enlarge; regenerate = regrow; gestation = pregnancy; lactate = produce milk.

summary: You can now name what the body is doing with exact HESI A2 process words, from ingesting a meal to excreting waste. You can also separate the sound-alike pairs the exam uses as distractors: excrete and secrete, ingest and digest, aspirate and expectorate, dilate and dilute.

A.q: The small intestine absorbs most of the nutrients from a meal. What is the best definition of the word "absorbs" in this sentence?
A.why: Absorb means to take in a substance through a surface or membrane.

whyNot.2: Storing keeps a substance; absorbing takes it in.
whyNot.3: Removing waste is excrete, the opposite direction.

A.q: Which word means "to break food down into substances the body can absorb"?
A.why: Digest means to break food down into substances the body can absorb.

whyNot.0: Ingest means to take in by swallowing, the digest look-alike.
whyNot.3: Secrete means to produce and release a substance.

A.q: The patient has not defecated in three days, so the nurse offered a stool softener. What is the best definition of the word "defecated" in this sentence?
A.why: Defecate means to pass feces from the bowel.

whyNot.1: Eating solid food is intake, not elimination.

B.q: A machine was used to ventilate the patient throughout the surgery. What is the best definition of the word "ventilate" in this sentence?
options: move air in and out of the lungs
B.why: Ventilate means to move air into and out of the lungs.

whyNot.1: Circulating room air is an everyday sense of ventilate, but this sentence is about the patient's lungs.
whyNot.2: Monitoring the heart is a different machine's job.
whyNot.3: Keeping a patient asleep is anesthesia.

B.q: Hours of hiking in the heat without water left Tyler with signs of dehydration. What is the best definition of the word "dehydration" in this sentence?
B.why: Dehydration is excessive loss of water from the body.

whyNot.0: Cramps may accompany it, but cramping is not the meaning of dehydration.
whyNot.3: High body temperature fits the heat loosely, but that is hyperthermia or fever.

B.q: Years of weightlifting caused hypertrophy of Marco's shoulder muscles. What is the best definition of the word "hypertrophy" in this sentence?
B.why: Hypertrophy is enlargement of a tissue or organ from growth of its cells.

whyNot.2: Weakness is the opposite of what weightlifting produces.

C.q: Which sentence uses the word "secrete" correctly?
options: The lungs secrete carbon dioxide as we exhale.
The thyroid gland secretes hormones into the blood.
The colon secretes feces out of the body.
The stomach secretes food into the intestine.
C.why: Secrete means to produce and release a useful substance; glands secrete hormones.

whyNot.0: Getting rid of carbon dioxide is excretion (exhalation), not secretion.
whyNot.2: Passing feces is defecation, a form of elimination, not secretion.
whyNot.3: The stomach empties food onward; it does not produce the food it passes on.

C.q: Some mothers continue to lactate for more than a year after giving birth. What is the best definition of the word "lactate" in this sentence?

whyNot.2: Weight loss fits the time after birth loosely, but it is not lactation.

C.q: The liver can regenerate after part of it is removed in surgery. What is the best definition of the word "regenerate" in this sentence?
C.why: Regenerate means to regrow or renew damaged or lost tissue.

whyNot.0: Wasting away is atrophy or degenerate.
whyNot.1: Scarring replaces tissue with scar, the opposite of true regrowth.
whyNot.3: Controlling is regulate, a look-alike word.

reteach.title: The body as a factory
reteach.question: If the body were a factory, which process word names each job: receiving goods, processing them, shipping products and hauling away trash?

blocks.body: Trucks unload raw goods at the dock: ingest. Machines break them into parts: digest. Parts move into the plant through the loading doors: absorb. The plant turns parts into products: metabolize. Finished products ship out to customers: secrete. Trash goes to the dump: excrete. Secrete ships something useful; excrete throws something away.

blocks.text: Shipping a product (secrete) and hauling trash (excrete) both send something out, so the HESI A2 pairs them. Ask: is it useful (secrete) or waste (excrete)?

explain.body: Ingest = take in by swallowing. Masticate = chew. Digest = break down. Absorb = take in through a membrane.

test.q: Which word means "to take into the body by swallowing"?
test.why: Ingest means to take into the body by swallowing.

whyNot.0: Inject means to force fluid in with a needle.
whyNot.1: Digest means to break food down.

explain.body: Excrete = eliminate waste. Secrete = produce and release a useful substance. Void = urinate. Defecate = pass feces. Expectorate = cough up mucus.

test.q: Which word means "to eliminate waste from the body"?
test.why: Excrete means to eliminate waste from the body.

whyNot.1: Secrete means to produce and release a useful substance.
whyNot.2: Absorb means to take in, the opposite direction.
whyNot.3: Ingest means to take in by swallowing.

explain.body: Dilate = widen. Constrict = narrow. Coagulate = clot. Perfusion = blood flow through tissue.

test.why: Constrict means to make narrower or squeeze.

whyNot.0: Dilate means to widen, the opposite.
whyNot.2: Construct means to build; it only looks like constrict.
whyNot.3: Distend means to swell or stretch outward.

explain.body: Atrophy = wasting away. Hypertrophy = enlargement. Regenerate = regrow. Gestation = development in the uterus. Lactate = produce milk.

test.q: Which word means "wasting away of a body part"?
test.why: Atrophy is wasting away or shrinking of a body part, especially muscle.
